# `shell/echo-guide/EchoGuidePathfinder.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/shell/echo-guide/EchoGuidePathfinder.js`

_No file-level description found in source. Add one as a leading `/** ... */` JSDoc comment, or document it below._

## Functions

### `planEchoGuideRoute({ viewport, start, goal, obstacles = [], cellSize = DEFAULT_CELL_SIZE, actorRadius = DEFAULT_ACTOR_RADIUS, } = {})`

Plan a bounded, deterministic screen-space route for the Echo guide. The engine navigation grid uses x/z world coordinates. This adapter keeps that implementation authoritative and translates viewport y to grid z only at the boundary.

### `normalizeEchoGuideViewport(viewport)`

Normalize and bound a viewport without depending on DOM viewport objects.

### `normalizeEchoGuidePoint(point, viewport)`

Normalize a center point and clamp it to the supplied viewport.

### `normalizeEchoGuideSafeAreaInsets(value, viewport)`

Normalize physical viewport insets without trusting CSS or host values.

### `clampEchoGuidePointToSafeArea(point, viewport, safeAreaInsets = {}, actorRadius = DEFAULT_ACTOR_RADIUS,)`

Clamp an actor center to the usable viewport after safe-area insets.

### `snapEchoGuidePointToNearestEdge({ point, viewport, safeAreaInsets = {}, actorRadius = DEFAULT_ACTOR_RADIUS, edge = 'nearest', } = {})`

Snap a bounded actor center to its nearest usable viewport edge.

### `findEchoGuideRetreatPoint({ goal, viewport, safeAreaInsets = {}, protectedRects = [], actorRadius = DEFAULT_ACTOR_RADIUS, maxRings = DEFAULT_RETREAT_RINGS, } = {})`

Move a proposed actor center away from bounded protected rectangles. This is geometry-only: callers decide which owned DOM surfaces are protected.

### `normalizeEchoGuideObstacles(obstacles, viewport, actorRadius = DEFAULT_ACTOR_RADIUS)`

Normalize DOMRect-style or x/y/width/height obstacles, inflate them by the actor radius, clip them to the viewport, and return a stable ordering.

### `compressEchoGuideWaypoints(waypoints)`

Remove duplicate and collinear points while retaining all real turns.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
